title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: GRANDPA'S ACCORDION
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Gina Novak, thirty-six, who packs pretzels at a factory in Scranton, Pennsylvania.
Her grandma Stella turns ninety in March. And Stella wants a polka party.
One problem. The only polka player in the family was Grandpa Walt. And Walt is gone.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE CLOSET
segments.quote: Nothing in the world is worth having or worth doing unless it means effort, pain, difficulty.
segments.author: Theodore Roosevelt
lines: Grandpa's accordion had sat in a closet for twenty years. It weighed as much as a turkey.
Gina said, I'll play it. Grandma laughed so hard she had to sit down.
Gina remembered a line her dad kept on the fridge, from Theodore Roosevelt:
Nothing in the world is worth having or worth doing unless it means effort, pain, difficulty.
So she carried that turkey home.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE NEIGHBOR
segments.quote: One half of the world cannot understand the pleasures of the other.
segments.author: Jane Austen
lines: Her first song sounded like a goose stuck in a revolving door.
Mr. Dombrowski next door pounded on the wall. His dog howled along.
Gina thought of a line from Jane Austen, her favorite writer:
One half of the world cannot understand the pleasures of the other.
So she let that half sleep. She practiced in her car at lunch, in the factory parking lot.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE TEACHER
segments.quote: A legend is an old man with a cane known for what he used to do. I'm still doing it.
segments.author: Miles Davis
lines: She needed a teacher. Frank Wozniak, eighty-four, had played in Grandpa's old band.
Gina asked if he was retired. Frank smiled and quoted the jazz great Miles Davis:
A legend is an old man with a cane known for what he used to do. I'm still doing it.
Then he cleared his kitchen table. Lessons were every Tuesday. Pay was pierogi.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: ONE SONG
segments.quote: I only know two pieces, one is 'Clair de Lune', the other one isn't.
segments.author: Victor Borge
lines: Gina wanted to learn twenty songs. Frank said no. Learn one. Learn it well.
He quoted the funny piano man Victor Borge:
I only know two pieces, one is 'Clair de Lune', the other one isn't.
So Gina picked one song, Grandpa's favorite polka. She played it every day for two months.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE FISH FRY
segments.quote: Every strike brings me closer to the next home run.
segments.author: Babe Ruth
lines: Frank booked her a tryout at the Friday fish fry at the VFW hall.
Halfway through, her strap snapped. She played three wrong notes in a row.
Then she saw Frank's old Yankees cap and remembered Babe Ruth:
Every strike brings me closer to the next home run.
So she started again, from the top. By the end, two old couples were dancing.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE PARTY
segments.quote: If this isn't nice, I don't know what is.
segments.author: Kurt Vonnegut
lines: March came. Sixty relatives packed the hall. Gina's hands shook. She played anyway.
Grandma Stella danced with Frank. She was ninety. He was eighty-four. Nobody sat down.
Then Grandma whispered the line from her favorite writer, Kurt Vonnegut:
If this isn't nice, I don't know what is.
So Gina played Grandpa's song again. And again. Four times.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Do the hard thing. Respect others. Find a teacher. Go deep. Start again. Enjoy it.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Do the hard thing. Respect others. Find a teacher. Go deep. Start again. Enjoy it.
I tried the accordion once myself. My neighbors moved.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
